properties.value: {"evidence": "*Same field report, 2026-08-03, and reproduced in this repo while filing these rows.* In the field: open_questions at session start returned {\"count\":0,\"items\":[]}, and loop_status in the very next call reported 11 structural defects, 3 capabilities claiming realized with no passing check, and 17 built capabilities never checked against reality. Reproduced here 2026-08-04 \u2014 open_questions returned 0 while loop_status reported 2 outstanding structural defects: the same shape at smaller scale, so this is not a property of one messy graph. Both answers are true and they answer different questions; the problem is purely that the call a session runs first is the one that looks like an all-clear, and the hook's own wording points at it. Fix is small and needs no schema: have open_questions name the other outstanding counts when they are non-zero \u2014 even *\"0 questions; loop_status reports 31 other items\"* \u2014 so an empty result cannot be read as an empty loop.
